modules.name: Learn
modules.title: -ing and -ed Adjective Lessons
modules.instructions: Master the cause-effect distinction: -ing adjectives describe characteristics of a person, thing, or situation; -ed adjectives describe how a person feels or is affected. Understand the full set of common -ing/-ed pairs and apply them correctly.

modules.name: Write
modules.title: Writing Practice
modules.instructions: Write sentences using -ing adjectives for causes and -ed adjectives for feelings. Apply correct pairs in contexts like film reviews, personal reactions, and situation descriptions.

modules.name: Play
modules.title: Grammar Games
modules.instructions: Play games to practice choosing between the -ing cause form and the -ed effect form. Recognize the signal words that show whether you need a cause or an effect adjective.

modules.name: Apply
modules.title: -ing/-ed Adjectives Challenge
modules.instructions: Apply -ing and -ed adjective pairs correctly in sentences. Master advanced pairs including hypnotizing/hypnotized, rewarding/rewarded, and tempting/tempted.

categories.title: Sentence Starters / Useful Phrases
words: Contrast: Although the news was ___ [ing], I wasn't ___ [ed].
Conditional: If something is [boring], you feel [bored].
Time clause: After watching the ___ film, I felt ___.
Emphatic: It was the most ___ [ing] experience I've ever had!
